title: Bound from the split equation
statement: Let $a,c,m,n$ be natural numbers. If the exponential-split search with coefficient $1$, degree $c$, and length $m$ returns $n$, then $a\cdot 2^{n^c}\le a\cdot m$.
hypotheses_covered: the exponential-split search with coefficient $1$, degree $c$, and length $m$ returns $n$
replaced:
If the exponential-split search with coefficient one returns $n$ on a length
$m$, then $a \cdot 2^{n^c} \le a \cdot m$ for every constant $a$, including
degree zero.
